subject: Stakeholder sweep: rollout guardrails, enablement owners, and canary cadence
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder sweep: rollout guardrails, enablement owners, and canary cadence

Team —

Quick sync request as we finalise the rollout for the Atlas integration next month. Goal is to lock on three things before Friday:

- Canary cadence (who/when we flip traffic, rollback window)
- Enablement owners (docs, customer training, CS handoff)
- Exception/guardrail list (what triggers a pause vs. fast follow)

I attached a first-pass timeline and the enablement slide deck. Can each of you reply with:
1) your primary owner (if not you already) for enablement artifacts,
2) any hard constraints (SLO/dependency) we should bake into the canary, and
3) one outstanding doc or decision we must close this week.

Jordan — looping you so Maple Health has visibility; we expect the first canary on week 1 of next month and want to coordinate training.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Launches
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@maplehealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder sweep: rollout guardrails, enablement owners, and canary cadence

Marissa —

Short answers:
1) Enablement owner: Priyom (I will own the customer-facing enablement slide deck and the quickstart doc).
2) Hard constraints: we need a 15-minute median tail lat < 300ms for core inference at expected canary QPS (I dropped numbers into the timeline file). If we hit >500ms median during the canary, we should pause and collect traces. Also need DB migration to complete (DB-1223) before a full rollout.
3) Outstanding decision: final verbatim for the FAQ regarding data retention — legal is still reviewing the short copy.

I'll also schedule a 30-min triage slot tomorrow (April 21 9:00am PT) to walk the canary plan.

-priyom

--
Priyom Das
Manager, Developer Enablement
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Stakeholder sweep: rollout guardrails, enablement owners, and canary cadence

Adding details from CS/Onboarding:

- Enablement owner: Laura will own the CS playbook and two live training sessions (canary week + pre-rollout).
- Constraints: CS needs an internal test tenant with production-like data by April 28 to rehearse failover and classification errors. If that's not ready, we push the canary by one week.
- Outstanding doc: API change log — engineering to confirm the stable fields list (Vivek, can you confirm by EOD?).

Jordan — can you confirm preferred time for the training session? We can do a 45-min customer walk-through during the canary week.

-Laura

Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder sweep: rollout guardrails, enablement owners, and canary cadence

Vivek here — engineer response:

- API change log: confirmed. I'll drop the stable-fields.diff into the Drive folder by EOD today.
- Canary cadence proposal: 3 phased canaries over 2 weeks: 1% -> 10% -> 30% traffic. Rollback window 60 minutes after observing the first regression signal (latency or error-rate spike).
- Guardrails: automatic fallback to hosted small-model variant if error-rate > 2% for 10 minutes, plus an automated alert to on-call infra.

Notes on infra cost: 30% traffic will require burst capacity; cost estimate in the timeline spreadsheet is optimistic — FYI for finance.

-Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks everyone — this looks good. A couple of asks from Maple Health: 

- Can the training be scheduled on Tue May 5 at 11am ET? That would work best for our ops and clinical teams.
- For the failover rehearsals, we need a runbook with step-by-step customer actions (who we call, expected system behaviour). Could Redwood produce a one-page runbook we can keep in our runbook binder?

We are OK with the 1% -> 10% -> 30% cadence pending the DB migration. Please flag if the week-of May 3 timeline slips.

—Jordan
